title: A tensor section has affine nonvanishing locus when one factor does
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_n$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $t_i$ be global sections of $\mathcal L_i$. Write $\tau=t_1\otimes\cdots\otimes t_n$ for the induced global section of the tensor product $\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and let $X_{t_i}$ and $X_\tau$ be their nonvanishing loci [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X_\tau=\bigcap_i X_{t_i}$. If one $X_{t_i}$ is affine, then $X_\tau$ is affine.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NC proof, sentence invoking Properties Lemma 28.27.4

proof.text: At a point $x$ of $X$, each fibre $\mathcal L_i(x)$ is one-dimensional over $\kappa(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], the tensor product is invertible and the value of $\tau$ in its fibre is $t_1(x)\otimes\cdots\otimes t_n(x)$. A pure tensor of vectors in one-dimensional vector spaces over a field is nonzero exactly when every factor is nonzero: choose a basis in each fibre and multiply the scalar coordinates. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], nonzero fibre value is exactly membership in the nonvanishing locus. Thus $x\in X_\tau$ iff $x\in X_{t_i}$ for every $i$, proving the equality of opens.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CT (tensor products of invertible modules), Lemma 01CB (fibre tensor identity), and Lemma 01CY (fibre criterion for nonvanishing)

proof.text: Suppose $X_{t_j}$ is affine for some index $j$. Starting with $U=X_{t_j}$, intersect successively with each of the finitely many remaining opens $X_{t_i}$. At every stage $U$ is an affine open of $X$, so [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open], applied to $\mathcal L_i$ and $t_i$, says $U\cap X_{t_i}$ is affine. After the last intersection, the resulting affine open is $\bigcap_i X_{t_i}=X_\tau$ by step 1.
